messages:
Sam (Sales): FYI CoralPay just escalated — EU throughput tanked after this morning's rollout. They report p95 ~180ms -> ~620ms and requests/sec dropped ~60%. Req id 8a7f3c. They're on Dedicated pool dp-67.
Rachel (Support): Customer sent screenshots of Console and a short clip. Spike starts ~2025-03-12T09:12Z. Ticket #7894 created, customer says outage impacts checkout.
Maya (PM): What's their SLA/contract? Do we have an agreement for Dedicated burst capacity? Need scope: temporary mitigation vs long-term fix. @Jon @Li, can you triage?
Jon (Eng): On it. Can you paste the route config or the exact route they hit? Also any hints if model fallback happened (different model variant)?
Rachel (Support): Route: POST /v1/chat -> route id r-143e. Screenshot shows model pinned to `redwood-large-v1` but console shows fallback logs.
Li (Infra): I see a prod deploy at 2025-03-12T09:05 UTC that touched routing routing/queueing logic (release/canary -> prod). deploy-bot confirms: "canary->prod by ci/cd at 09:05". Node gpu-node-19 queue depth increased around 09:10.
deploy-bot: canary->prod: release/2025-03-12.
Jon (Eng): paste from our edge logs:
```
2025-03-12T09:12:14Z ERROR serve: request queued 0.63s route=/v1/chat model=redwood-large-v1 pool=dp-67 req=8a7f3c
2025-03-12T09:12:20Z WARN batching: batch_size target decreased from 6 -> 2 for route=r-143e
2025-03-12T09:12:21Z INFO routing: fallback to redwood-medium-quant for req=8a7f3c
```
Jon (Eng): Looks like the routing change caused batching to shrink and fallback happened -> increased per-token overhead. That explains throughput drain.
Sam (Sales): Customer wants immediate mitigation — can we pin them to a low-latency variant or bump burst capacity while we investigate?
Maya (PM): For customers on Dedicated with contractual SLAs we prioritize restoration. Decision: try soft mitigation first (pin to fast-variant + increase burst for dp-67) and monitor for 30m. If no improvement, rollback routing change. @Jon take lead.
Jon (Eng): Doing a targeted canary: will route only dp-67 traffic to `redwood-large-v1-fastfallback` (non-quant) and temporarily set min_batch_size=4 for that tenant. Applying now.
Jon (Eng): applied canary at 2025-03-12T09:18 UTC, monitoring p95.
Jon (Eng): update — p95 dropped to ~190ms within 4m, requests/sec recovering to 95% of baseline.
Rachel (Support): Customer confirmed noticeable improvement in their test account. They asked for ETA on a permanent fix.
Sam (Sales): They want written confirmation and a short-term SLA adjustment while we patch. I'll draft and send.
Maya (PM): Good. Next steps: 1) Postmortem to capture root cause + regression guardrails. 2) Product decision: add per-tenant burst overrides and safe-mode routing flag to roadmap. 3) Engineering: revert routing change or harden the batching heuristics.
Jon (Eng): Agree. I'll open an internal bug with logs, include timeline and minimal repro. Proposing a safe rollback for routing change if tests show instability in other tenants.
Li (Infra): Also recommend we add better signals on queue depth -> auto-escalate to reroute before fallback happens. I'll file infra action item.
Maya (PM): Assign follow-up: eng-platform for batching heuristics (owner: Jon), infra for queue triggers (owner: Li), product for roadmap item (owner: Maya). Priority: P1 for immediate fix window, P2 for roadmap feature.
Sam (Sales): Customer happy for now, will validate over next 30m and revert if anything odd. I'll keep them updated.
Rachel (Support): Closing the active alert once customer confirms stable for 30m, keep the ticket open for postmortem notes.
Jon (Eng): Noted. I'll capture canary config + rollback plan in the bug.
Maya (PM): Thanks team. We'll discuss scope & acceptance criteria for the per-tenant burst override during next planning — need ETA estimate from Jon and Li.
Sam (Sales): Customer asked if this can be prioritized into next sprint if we can't guarantee stability long-term. I'll flag as potential contract impact.
Maya (PM): Understood. We'll negotiate scope vs timeline in roadmap session.
Rachel (Support): Customer ping: "Thanks — system looks normal again, will confirm tomorrow AM." :thumbsup:
Sam (Sales): Marking this as handoff complete for now. Follow-up: roadmap item and infra trigger.
Maya (PM): Creating backlog ticket now: "per-tenant burst controls + routing safe-mode" and linking bug.
Jon (Eng): adding notes and logs to the bug.
Li (Infra): I'll draft the trigger playbook for queue-depth alerts.
Maya (PM): Great. Closing thread — reopen if regression resurfaces. :eyes:
